extracted.intended_audience: students/scholars reading a historical/medieval arithmetic treatise (number theory/arithmetic practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive treatise on properties and manipulations of numbers (perfect numbers, binary/quaternary/octonary relations, division into parts), giving procedures to generate, decompose and classify numbers. Contains step-by-step algorithms (in prose) and many illustrative numeric examples/series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule to generate perfect numbers by successive duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Quando i numeri continuamente dupli per ordine fen^a falto ... produce numeri perfetti. Quella e la regola che da edoclude altro numero perfecto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: duplicate numbers successively (2, 4, 8, 16, ...) and use the sequence of duplicates and their sums/products in a prescribed pattern to obtain a 'numero perfecto'. The text repeatedly instructs duplicating 'per ordine' and assembling duplicates (multiplying the last duplicate by the earlier ones or adding appropriate duplicates) to form perfect numbers; examples and long numeric sequences are given in the margin and body to illustrate the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for finding fractional parts via successive halving (binary partitioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partilo per 2 ... prendi la mita de quella mita ancona partédolo in 2 ... e cosi in infinitum; piglia la i. de qllo ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain successive fractional parts of a number, repeatedly divide by 2 (halves), then by 2 again (quarters), and so on; collect the halves/quarters/etc as named parts (mita, octava parte, decima parte, etc.). The treatise shows how to continue these halvings to extract the 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, ... parts and records numeric examples (long sequences like '225'... and many later extractions) demonstrating the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to express a number as a sum of binary-indexed parts (binary expansion style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prendi la mita ... poi prendi la mita di quella ... e cosi ... la prima, seconda, terza parte del numero ... e componi numeri per potere ridurre e descrivere il totale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text prescribes extracting successive binary parts (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, ...) and using those parts (and their multiples) to reconstruct or analyse the whole number. It gives a step-by-step operational way to determine which fractional parts (and multiples thereof) occur in the decomposition and lists many constructed intermediate numbers as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of numbers by parity and by divisible equal parts (pariter / impariter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisiones: 'numero paro', 'pariter paro', 'pariter impari' etc.; si puo dividere a parti eguali e di nuovo le parti di quelle in do parti eguali in infinitum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines and distinguishes classes of numbers according to whether and how they can be divided into equal parts repeatedly (even/odd behavior). The treatise traces nomenclature (pariterpar o pariterimpar) and shows how successive equal partitions behave and are named when continued indefinitely or until reaching the unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination/denomination test by successive extraction of specific base parts (fenaria, octonaria, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Il numero puo essere giudicato perfecto per rispetto di la terminatione fenaria onero octonaria ... prima parte, seconda parte, quarta parte, ottava parte ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A method to test whether a number 'terminates' in a given base (e.g., in binary, octal) by repeatedly taking prescribed fractional parts (half, quarter, eighth, etc.) and checking rearrangements/denominations. The text prescribes taking successive fractional parts (1/4, 1/8, 1/16, ...) and using them to obtain the unit or to determine the 'terminazione' relative to various bases; examples and stepwise extractions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping and relations among positional bases (binary, quaternary, octonary, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coppo el binario, coppio el quaternario, poi el octonario ... 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 ... il copio al quale 52 x poi 64 c poi ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the multiplicative relationships between bases (binary->quaternary->octonary etc.) and how parts in one base correspond to parts in another. The treatise enumerates sequences 2,4,8,16,32,64... and shows how a given part in one system receives a denomination when viewed in a larger base (e.g., how a quarter relates to an eighth, etc.), with worked examples showing denominational names and transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic method for producing many derived parts and assembling them into ordered series
rubrics_metrics.description: La regola: duplica continuamente, raccoglierli e vedere la summa che fanno ... farai per l'altro e poi que' altri quati ne vogliano in infinitum ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an explicit iterative (algorithmic) process: duplicate, collect duplicates, form sums/products, and continue the process to produce an ordered infinite family of derived numbers/parts. The text lists explicit intermediate results and long numerical series (including many powers of two and composite intermediate numbers) as illustrations of repeated application of the algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical numeric procedures and worked examples for decomposition and recomposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise provides many long worked numeric examples showing the decomposition of large numbers into binary/quaternary parts and their recomposition. These examples function as practical guidance on applying the described procedures; readers are expected to follow the same halving/duplication/extraction steps on their own numbers.
